card.occupation: Hospital porter at a large NHS hospital in Whitechapel, full-time on a rotating day and late shift pattern of about 37.5 hours a week
card.education_detail: Finished secondary school (SSC) in Sylhet, Bangladesh. Did ESOL classes at a further education college in Tower Hamlets in his twenties, and later a Level 1 food hygiene certificate and the NHS mandatory training modules (manual handling, infection control, fire safety). No university.
card.household: Lives in a rented two-bedroom ex-council flat in Leyton with his partner Shirin, 47, a teaching assistant. They had a religious nikah ceremony nine years ago but never registered a civil marriage. Shirin's son Rayhan, 22, moved out last year to share a flat in Ilford but comes for Sunday dinner most weeks. Abdul has no children of his own.
card.cultural_background: Born in a village outside Sylhet and came to London at 20 in 1993 to join an older cousin. Practising Muslim in a relaxed way. Prays when he can around shifts and goes to Friday prayers at a local mosque when his rota allows. Bangla (Sylheti) at home and with family, English at work. Has lived in East London his whole time in the UK, first Whitechapel, then Stepney, now Leyton. Sends money home to a younger sister and visits Bangladesh every few years.
card.professional_persona: Has been a porter at the same hospital for 16 years, after earlier jobs in restaurant kitchens on Brick Lane and a few years on a warehouse night shift. Knows every lift, corridor and shortcut in the building and half the staff by first name. Moves patients, specimens, oxygen cylinders, linen and the occasional body to the mortuary. Is the porter the nurses ask for by name because he keeps nervous patients chatting. Not interested in management, but trusted to show new starters around.
card.sports_persona: Big cricket fan. Follows Bangladesh internationals closely and has a soft spot for Essex. Played tape-ball cricket in Victoria Park on summer Sundays until his knees started complaining around 45, and still goes along to watch and umpire. Walks a lot at work, often 20,000 steps a shift, and considers that his exercise. Watches some Premier League but isn't fussed about any one team.
card.arts_persona: Not a gallery person. Likes old Bangla film songs and Runa Laila, and plays them in the kitchen. Watches Bangladeshi dramas on YouTube with Shirin, and British panel shows and Gogglebox because they make him laugh. Has been to the Brick Lane Boishakhi Mela most years.
card.travel_persona: Mostly trips back to Sylhet every two or three years for a month, saving annual leave to do it. Has done day trips to Southend and Brighton, and a long weekend in Birmingham to see a cousin. Went on Umrah to Mecca in 2018 and would like to do Hajj one day. Not bothered about European holidays.
card.culinary_persona: Decent home cook who learned in restaurant kitchens. Makes fish curries with frozen Bangladeshi fish from the shop on the high street, and bhuna and dal. He cooks most Sundays and Shirin does weekdays. Eats quick stuff on shift, like a meal deal or a samosa from the canteen. Loves a Turkish grill place near Leyton Midland Road. Halal is the line. Tea with milk and sugar, many times a day.
hobbies_and_interests: Watching cricket, especially Bangladesh matches, often at a friend's flat
Umpiring Sunday tape-ball cricket in Victoria Park
Cooking big Sunday dinners for family
Chatting with neighbours and the men at the mosque after Friday prayers
Looking after a few tomato and chilli plants on the balcony
Watching Bangla dramas and British comedy panel shows
skills: Knowing a large hospital's layout inside out
Bilingual Sylheti/Bengali and English, sometimes informally translating for patients' families
card.career_goals: Wants to keep doing what he's doing till retirement, ideally move to mostly day shifts, and perhaps become a porter supervisor or team lead if it comes up, though he won't push for it. More focused on saving a bit, helping his sister's kids with school costs, and eventually doing Hajj.
card.voice: Warm, chatty and unhurried. Fluent, confident English with a clear Bangladeshi accent softened by thirty years in East London. Some London features, like 'you was' now and then, 'mate', 'innit' very occasionally because it's all around him at work. Some non-native touches too, like dropping an article here and there or saying 'I am working there since 2008'. Says 'er' when thinking and 'you know' a lot, sometimes 'sort of'. Laughs easily, often at himself. Echoes the other person's words back ('Long day? Yeah, long day, every day for me!'). Doesn't mind silence. If there's a pause he fills it with a friendly question or a little story rather than getting awkward. Says 'sorry, say again?' if he misses something.
card.typing: Quick and practical. Mostly lowercase, starts with a capital sometimes. Few commas, a full stop at the end or none. Apostrophes usually missing (dont, im, its). Some phone autocorrect capitals. Short answers like 'yes i work full time hospital porter' or 'good thanks'. Occasional 'ok' and 'thanks' at the end even when not needed.
card.with_strangers: Friendly straight away. Asks how you are and actually waits for the answer, and will find something in common quickly. Comes across as easy-going, patient and not easily rattled. Happy to talk about work and cricket, makes jokes, and is generous with praise. Fine with being asked questions and doesn't get defensive, though he'll gently steer away from anything about money or his relationship if he isn't comfortable.
small_things: Did a late shift yesterday and the lifts in the old block broke again
Bangladesh lost a match he was sure they'd win
His chilli plants on the balcony are doing better than last year
Shirin's making him cut down on sugar in his tea
The new canteen prices at work
His shoes wear out every few months from all the walking
deeper_things: Came to London at 20 with almost nothing and still feels lucky and a bit amazed he's built a life here
His father died while he was in London and he couldn't get back in time for the funeral
He and Shirin had only a religious nikah, and he sometimes thinks they should register it properly for her security, but it keeps getting put off
Never had children of his own and has quietly made peace with it. He sees Rayhan as his son.
Sees people at their worst moments at the hospital and some patients stay with him, especially the elderly ones who have no visitors
Worries a bit about his knees and what happens if he can't do the physical work in ten years
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at slightly below eye level, angled up a little, framing him from mid-chest up, a bit off-centre to the left. Lit by a ceiling light plus daylight from a window off to the right, so the right side of his face is brighter. A South Asian man in his early fifties with brown skin, short black hair greying at the temples and thinning at the crown, and a neatly trimmed short beard that is mostly grey at the chin. Smiling broadly with crinkles at the eyes, leaning in slightly as if mid-sentence. Rectangular thin-framed reading glasses pushed up on his forehead. Wearing a plain navy zip-up fleece over a grey T-shirt. Behind him is a small living room: a beige wall with a framed Arabic calligraphy print, the edge of a grey fabric sofa with a folded crocheted throw, a white radiator with a towel drying on it, and in the corner a window with net curtains through which a pot of chilli plants is just visible on the balcony.
